mode_evidence: The Manresa shape appeared 'in the courtyard before him' on moonlit nights and he 'gazed at it' (outward, perceptual-sounding); the white rays and the white body of Christ are seen 'with the eyes of his soul'; the meat dish 'he appeared to see it with his eyes'. Ignatius himself does not settle where the seeing happens.
onset_evidence: No induction is taught. Visions arose during seven hours of daily prayer, scourging, fasting and vigils, and at night on retiring. A lamp-like illumination came while sitting gazing at a river with no image. The only use for a seer is discernment, not onset.

conditions.posture: Prayer on bended knees seven hours a day.
conditions.gaze_or_eye_position: Once sat and gazed at deep flowing water.
conditions.setting: Hospital courtyard in moonlight; cell; church at Mass.
conditions.duration_and_schedule: Months at Manresa; the white body seen perhaps twenty or forty times.
conditions.other: Learned discernment of spirits from experience.

stages.label: the beautiful shape
stages.description: Indistinct, symmetrical, serpent-like with glittering 'eyes that were not eyes', gave consolation; later seen gleaming with many eyes.

stages.label: illumination at the river
stages.description: No vision, but a lasting new light of understanding.

what_to_do_with_light: Test by effect and colour: the shape lost its colour near the cross, so he judged it of the devil and dispelled it with his staff. The white body and rays he accepted and trusted.
obstacles_and_fixes: Doubted whether night illuminations were from the good spirit: shortened vigil and gave more time to sleep.
cautions: A consoling, beautiful vision can be the devil's; discern by its effects and by what it does near holy signs.
interpretation: Visions are grace or diabolic according to discernment of effects; the river illumination is light of understanding.
practice_summary: Ignatius gives testimony, not a method. At Manresa he prayed seven hours daily on his knees, fasted, scourged himself and kept vigils. On retiring, illuminations and consolations came, to the point that he cut sleep. In moonlight a beautiful indistinct shape appeared in the courtyard; the oftener he saw it the greater his joy. Later he saw white rays at the elevation of the Host and the humanity of Christ as a white body, many times, with the eyes of the soul. He treated them by discernment: he asked whether he was left joyful or sad, doubted vigils that took his sleep, and when the shape lost its colour near a cross, he judged it the devil's and drove it off with his staff. Seated by a river he received a deep illumination without any image.
